name: California
source: California Franchise Tax Board 2025 Form 540 tax rate schedules X and Y, standard deduction and exemption credits (the newest published: FTB releases the 2026 indexed amounts in late December 2026), read through search extracts because ftb.ca.gov refused the fetch; second sources: TaxAct and Taxstra 2025 California guides, Plante Moran SALT advisor September 2025; the 1% Behavioral (Mental) Health Services Tax over 1,000,000 is folded into the brackets

state_base.note: California does not recognise HSAs, so HSA deposits are added back to the income it taxes; 401(k) deferrals and deductible Traditional IRA deposits follow the federal treatment (confirmed primary: https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-ca-instructions.html, validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

exemption_credits.note: 2025 exemption credits: 153 personal (306 joint), 153 more per person aged 65 or older, 475 per dependent (FTB 2EZ tables and TaxAct; Plante Moran gives 307 joint). Not modelled: the credits shrink by 6 per 2,500 (1,250 separate) of federal AGI above 252,203 single and 504,411 joint (2025 Form 540 booklet, https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-booklet.html, validation run 2, 2026-10-22), so the file slightly undertaxes a high-income return.

estate_inheritance.check_at: California Revenue and Taxation Code 13301-13304 (estate tax tied to the federal state death tax credit)
estate_inheritance.note: California levies no estate tax and no inheritance tax (its pick-up estate tax ended with the federal state death tax credit in 2005; the inheritance tax was repealed by Proposition 6 in 1982).

social_security.note: California does not tax Social Security benefits; it is not among the states that tax them in Kiplinger 2026 (https://www.kiplinger.com/taxes/states-that-tax-social-security-benefits) and AARP, as listed in .claude/state/research/state-costs.md. Confirmed primary on https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2025/2025-540-ca-instructions.html (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

local_income_tax.check_at: California State Controller city and county tax pages
local_income_tax.note: California cities and counties levy no personal income tax; San Francisco's and Los Angeles's business and payroll taxes fall on employers (state-costs.csv local_income_tax, from memory).

sales_tax.check_at: California revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: 0.0903 from the state's own source (California: sales or use tax on a car at the general rate of the buyer's place, so the combined rate (https://cdtfa.ca.gov/industry/vehicles-vessels-aircraft/vehicles.htm, validation run 3)). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: no); research note: Food products for home consumption exempt from state and local (Bradley-Burns and district) tax. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Confirmed primary on the Census ACS 2024 1-year tables (https://data.census.gov/api/access/data/table?id=ACSDT1Y2024.B25090&g=040XX00US06, validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.check_at: https://www.dmv.ca.gov (DMV collections report and vehicle registration fee calculator)
car_taxes.source: California DMV collections report, fiscal year 2024-25 (registration fees 4,287.3 million and Vehicle License Fee 3,764.8 million) and DMV estimated fee-paid registrations by county, 2025 (about 35.5 million), read through search extracts
car_taxes.note: Registration fees plus the Vehicle License Fee (0.65% of the vehicle's value) per fee-paid vehicle: (4,287.3 + 3,764.8) million / 35.5 million, about 227 a year. An average over every fee-paid vehicle (trucks, trailers and motorcycles included), so unconfirmed for a typical car; a 30,000 car pays about 195 of VLF plus about 150 of fees. Hand-set in s294; importStateCosts.py writes 0 here again if rerun for CA. Accepted: low impact (triage 2026-10-23): Derived from DMV collections / registrations: sound method.

fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel: 0.634 from 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30 (0.612 before; about 0.623 averaged over 2026); average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Price: 4.526, EIA California regular retail, 2024 annual (2025: 4.410) (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, California insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
